title: Liquid-glass pill navigation on a phone, cropped close-up
contains_third_party_content: A photo of a person (dark silhouette) is in the background.

color.method: Pixel sampling via median-cut quantization of the supplied JPEG/GIF (compressed images, so values are approximate within a few units). Entries marked 'approx' were judged by eye, not sampled.
color.roles: Cyan field against near-black photo; the glass control borrows the colors behind it.

observed.layout: Cropped to a phone's bottom-left corner. A large translucent rounded 'bubble' (selected tab) with a layered, thick-edge look overlaps a wider translucent bar containing white icons (camera, trophy). A small glass circle with a lightning icon floats mid-screen. The home indicator is visible.
observed.hierarchy: The selected bubble is the largest and most refractive object; the bar is a thin strip.
observed.materials: Translucent glass with bright edge highlights, visible thickness, and color tinting from the background; the pill appears to bend what is behind it.

interpretation.aesthetic: Liquid-glass / refractive glassmorphism, closer to physical glass than frosted blur.
implementation_notes: Real refraction is not possible with plain CSS blur; web approximations combine backdrop-filter with SVG displacement filters (limited browser support) or pre-rendered assets.
Native platforms increasingly ship a system glass material, which is the practical route for production apps.
Apparent thickness comes from a lighter inner edge plus offset shadow.
interpretation.caveat: Platform claims are general knowledge and may need checking against current docs; the creator's method is unknown.

concept_work.essence: The selected tab is a lens, a physical-feeling piece of glass that sits over the bar.
what_makes_it_work: Color of the glass adapts to the content behind it, which ties UI to context.
Larger selected element gives clear state.
gaps_to_make_it_work: Contrast of icons depends on whatever is behind the glass, which varies.
Refraction and blur are expensive on lower-end devices.
The crop shows too little to judge the whole layout.

lessons: Glass that depends on its backdrop needs a contrast guarantee (scrim or adaptive tint).
Refraction is a high-effect/high-cost technique; plan a flat fallback.
